title: Proactive Hunger Mitigator: Queue Sampler + TTL for Cold KV Pins
author: Ava Martinez
release_notes: Improves continuous-batcher fairness by introducing a probabilistic queue sampler and per-key TTL on KV cache pins to prevent starvation of low-weight requesters; reduces tail latency spikes and reduces long-lived cache pin buildup.
description: Context: In high-concurrency, mixed-weight workloads we observed long-lived KV pin clusters and unlucky queue ordering causing starvation of occasional low-weight traffic and microbursts that bypass batching fairness; this produced 95th/99th tail regressions on multi-tenant hosts. Motivation: Rather than hard-demoting flows or introducing heavyweight admission controls, this change adds a lightweight probabilistic sampler to the continuous-batcher queue plus a configurable TTL for KV cache pins so stale pins are evicted proactively. Summary of changes: 1) Add queue_sampler component that periodically samples queued requests and nudges under-served requesters toward priority slots using a randomized jittered backoff to avoid synchronized probes. 2) Wire sampler into scheduler decision path with a low-overhead path that only touches head-of-queue metadata to keep hot paths fast. 3) Introduce per-key pin_ttl and a soft-eviction policy in runtime/kv/cache_manager to age KV pins that have not been accessed by multiple windows, plus a pin_renew hook when requests observe repeated hits. 4) Add metrics and tracing: sampler.probes, sampler.nudges, kv.pin_ttl_evictions, kv.pin_renewals, and a sampler_latency histogram. 5) Provide a set of tunable knobs exposed through the console and runtime flags: sampler_min_interval_ms, sampler_probe_rate, pin_ttl_ms, pin_renew_threshold, sampler_jitter_pct. Implementation notes: The sampler uses an exponential backoff schedule per-cohort to limit probe volume under overload and a tiny bloom-style recent-sample filter to avoid reprobing the same queue item within a short interval. Pin TTL is intentionally conservative (default 5m) and only triggers soft-eviction that yields pins back to the allocator while allowing a fast re-pin on demand. Testing: Unit tests for sampler scheduling, filter correctness, and pin soft-eviction were added. Integration tests simulate mixed-weight flows and validate no regressions in aggregate throughput. Load experiments on staging used a synthetic 50/50 mix of heavy/ephemeral callers and a replay of production interleaving. Observed results: median latency unchanged, 95th down ~8-12% on heavy hosts, 99th down ~15-22% on hosts previously experiencing starvation, overall KV pin count per-host reduced by ~30% after warmup. Rollout plan: feature gated behind runtime flag and staged to Canary pool, then to 25% of capacity for 48h with observability dashboards and automated rollback triggers on error_rate or latency_breach. Related: builds on patterns from ENG-8421 and complements the batch-slot rebalancer. Checklist: [x] unit tests [x] integration tests [x] perf benchmarked in staging [x] metrics/dashboards added [x] feature-flagged [x] docs notes added. Motivation, design doc, and tuning guidance linked in Linear ENG-8421.

squash: Proactive Hunger Mitigator: Queue Sampler + TTL for Cold KV Pins

Adds queue sampler and pin_ttl soft-eviction to mitigate starvation in continuous batching. See ENG-8421 for design notes.
notes: Follow-up work: 1) expose sampler cohort thresholds in console (ENG-8670), 2) consider adaptive pin_ttl based on host memory pressure, 3) evaluate interaction with ranker-driven coalescing.
